# Leapstone

> Leapstone is a free app to play Chinese checkers and Halma on a 3D board in red lacquer and gold. Play the computer, or play online with friends through an invite link. No ads, no payments, no tracking. You choose a player name; there is no email address or password.

Leapstone is available on the App Store (iPhone), on Google Play (Android) at https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=nl.leapstone.app, and in the browser at https://playleapstone.com/play/. It is made by William Visser. The app and the browser game are in 43 languages; they start in the language of the device, and you can pick another one. The landing page, the Chinese checkers and Halma rules, the Sternhalma page and the guides for strategy and for 2 players exist in the same 43 languages, with the same content (Chinees dammen is the Dutch name of Chinese checkers, Sternhalma the German one). The guides "Halma vs Chinese checkers" and "Chinese checkers for 3 players" exist in English only.

## Facts

- Free, with no ads, no in-app purchases and no tracking. No account: you choose a player name, with no email address or password.
- Ways to play: against the computer (easy, normal or hard, no internet needed), with friends through an invite link (in the app or in the browser, with a time per move and chat), a quick online game against another player of your level (30 seconds per move; some online opponents may be computer players), and on one phone, passing it around.
- Leaderboard: players are listed by rating. Winning quick online games raises your rating; games with friends do not count.
- Puzzle of the day: a new puzzle every day, the same for everyone, to solve in as few moves as you can, with a streak of days in a row. It works without internet.
- Boards: the star board (Chinese checkers, 2, 3, 4 or 6 players, 10 pieces each) and the 16 by 16 square board (Halma, 2 or 4 players).
- The board is 3D, in red lacquer and gold, with lacquered pieces. You zoom in with two fingers; the board does not turn. There are no move hints.

## Pages

- [Leapstone](https://playleapstone.com/): what the app is, the ways to play and screenshots.
- [Play in your browser](https://playleapstone.com/play/): the web version of the game.
- [Chinese checkers rules](https://playleapstone.com/rules/chinese-checkers): how the pieces start, steps, jumps and chains of jumps, how to win with 2, 3, 4 or 6 players, tips, and short answers to common questions (number of players and marbles, jumping backwards, capturing, where the game comes from, where to play it online with friends).
- [Halma rules](https://playleapstone.com/rules/halma): the 16 by 16 square board for 2 or 4 players, steps and jumps in eight directions, how to win, tips, and short answers to common questions (players, pieces, who invented Halma, the difference with Chinese checkers, where to play it online).
- [Sternhalma](https://playleapstone.com/rules/sternhalma): what the name means, how Halma, Sternhalma and Chinese checkers relate, and how they differ.
- [Chinese checkers strategy](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-strategy): six tips for the star board with pictures: ladders, keeping pieces together, the middle, filling your goal, and blocking jumps.
- [Chinese checkers for 2 players](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-2-players): how a game for two works (setup, who moves first, winning and resigning), how it differs from 3, 4 or 6 players, and where to play it in Leapstone.
- [Chinese checkers for 3 players](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-3-players): how a game for three works (setup, the three empty goals, who moves first, winning and resigning), how it differs from a game for 2, and where to play it in Leapstone.
- [Chinese checkers for 4 players](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-4-players): how a game for four works (the board split into two pairs of points, the two empty points, who faces who, what changes in tactics, winning and resigning), and where to play it in Leapstone.
- [Chinese checkers for 6 players](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-6-players): how the full board works (all six points full, every goal is the start of the player across, the crowded middle, blocking, how long a game takes), and where to play it in Leapstone.
- [Halma vs Chinese checkers](https://playleapstone.com/guides/halma-vs-chinese-checkers): the square board against the star board, six or eight directions, players and pieces, and what is the same.
- [Chinese checkers opening moves](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-opening-moves): two openings with pictures (jump out of the second row and free the tip piece in 2 moves, or gain 13 rows in 4 moves with 4 different pieces), the 14 possible first moves, and mistakes in the first moves.
- [Play Chinese checkers online with friends](https://playleapstone.com/guides/play-chinese-checkers-online-with-friends): how to start an online game and send the invite link, how many players fit, the move time (15 seconds to 2 minutes, or none), playing with only a player name, and what happens when a friend drops out.
- [Can you move backwards in Chinese checkers?](https://playleapstone.com/rules/can-you-move-backwards-in-chinese-checkers): yes, a step or a jump works in all six directions; a picture of a backward jump that starts a chain.
- [Can you jump your own piece in Chinese checkers?](https://playleapstone.com/rules/can-you-jump-your-own-piece-in-chinese-checkers): yes, you may jump over any piece, also your own, if the spot behind it is empty; a picture and what stays the same.
- [Can you jump over your opponent in Chinese checkers?](https://playleapstone.com/rules/can-you-jump-over-your-opponent-in-chinese-checkers): yes, and nothing is captured: the piece you jump over stays; jumping is never required; a picture of two jumps over blue pieces.
- [Chinese checkers by the numbers](https://playleapstone.com/guides/chinese-checkers-by-the-numbers): the spots and pieces of the star board and the square board, the longest chain of jumps in one move (36) and the fewest moves for one player alone to cross the board (27), with how each number is counted and in which setup it holds.
